title: Review: Elastic strain energy; Structure of materials; Stress–strain and force–extension behaviour; Electric potential and potential energy; Newton's law of gravitation and field strength
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for Eduqas A-level Physics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: MT02-1#t2 term and clue written for the game; MT02-1#t4 term and clue written for the game; MT02-1#t3 term and clue written for the game; F04-1#t4 term and clue written for the game. Questions: C03-1#N.3, F04-1#N.10a, MT03-1#N.11, MT04-1#N.12, C03-1#N.10, F04-1#N.5a, MT03-1#N.4, MT04-1#N.9, C03-1#N.8a, MT03-1#N.8, MT04-1#N.11, MT04-1#N.6. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Elastic limit
items.clue: Largest force after which a wire still returns to its original length.

items.label: Hooke's law
items.clue: Statement that extension is directly proportional to the force applied.

items.label: Plastic deformation
items.clue: Change of shape that leaves a permanent extension when the load is removed.

items.label: Test charge
items.clue: Probe placed at P to sample V; its own size and sign do not affect the value.

questions.stem: Two objects exert gravitational forces of magnitude F on each other. The mass of each object is doubled, and the distance between their centres is tripled. What is the new magnitude of the gravitational force that each object exerts on the other?

In a region of uniform electric field of strength 4.0 × 10³ V m⁻¹ directed in the +x direction, point A at x = 0 has an electric potential of +500 V. What is the electric potential at point B, at x = 0.050 m?
A spring obeys Hooke's law. When it is compressed by 3.0 cm it stores 0.45 J. How much energy does it store when it is compressed by 4.5 cm?
questions.explanation: Energy ∝ (compression)². The compression is 1.5 times larger, so E = 0.45 × 1.5² = 1.0 J.

questions.stem: A crack is slowly growing across a sheet of acrylic, a brittle plastic, in a shop window. A technician drills a small round hole exactly at the crack's tip. The crack stops growing. Why?

options.text: The round hole replaces the sharp tip, so stress concentrates far less there.
Drilling lets the acrylic flow plastically, so its dislocations blunt the tip.
Removing material makes the sheet lighter, so the stress everywhere falls.
The hole squeezes the acrylic around it into compression, closing the crack.

questions.explanation: Stress crowds at a sharp tip, so bonds there break one by one. A rounded edge spreads the stress: the crack no longer grows.

questions.stem: Star X (mass 9.0 × 10³⁰ kg) and star Y (mass 1.0 × 10³⁰ kg) are 4.0 × 10¹¹ m apart, centre to centre. At one point on the line joining their centres, the resultant gravitational field strength is zero. How far is this point from the centre of X?
questions.explanation: GM_X/x² = GM_Y/(d − x)², so x/(d − x) = √(9.0/1.0) = 3, and x = ¾ × 4.0 × 10¹¹ = 3.0 × 10¹¹ m: nearer the smaller mass.

questions.stem: A point charge of +5.0 nC is fixed in place. A second charge of +2.0 nC is moved slowly from a point 0.30 m from the fixed charge to a point 0.10 m from it. Take 1/(4πε₀) = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻². What is the work done on the +2.0 nC charge by the external force?
A steel wire obeys Hooke's law. A tension of 60 N gives an extension of 1.2 mm. How much elastic strain energy does the wire store?
questions.explanation: Energy = ½ × force × extension = ½ × 60 × 1.2 × 10⁻³ = 0.036 J.

questions.stem: A toughened-glass panel survives knocks that would break ordinary glass. But if something sharp scratches deep into it, the whole panel shatters. Why?

options.text: The scratch reaches the inner glass, which is in tension, so a crack can run from it.
The scratch heats the glass so much that it undoes the toughening.
The compressed surface layer pushes the sides of the scratch apart.
Toughened glass is ductile, so only a deep scratch can start a crack.

questions.explanation: Toughening leaves the surface in compression and the core in tension. A flaw that reaches the core is under tension, and the crack runs.

questions.stem: The Earth exerts a gravitational force of 2.0 × 10²⁰ N on the Moon. The mass of the Moon is about 1.2% of the mass of the Earth. Which statement about the gravitational force that the Moon exerts on the Earth is correct?

options.text: It is 2.0 × 10²⁰ N, and it pulls the Earth towards the Moon.
It is about 1.2% of 2.0 × 10²⁰ N, as the Moon has far less mass.
It is zero, as a small body cannot attract a much larger one.
It is zero, as the Moon has no air and so has no gravity.

questions.stem: The spring in a toy dart launcher has a spring constant of 400 N m⁻¹. It is compressed by 0.030 m and then released, firing a dart of mass 0.012 kg horizontally. All the elastic potential energy is transferred to the dart's kinetic energy. What is the speed of the dart?
Rubber X has a large hysteresis loop; rubber Y has a very small one. A car tyre flexes and recovers on every turn of the wheel. Which rubber wastes less energy in the tyre, and why?

options.text: X, because its larger loop stores more energy to give back.
Y, because its loading curve must be steeper than X's.
Y, because less energy becomes internal energy in each flex.
X, because a larger loop means the rubber stretches less.

questions.explanation: Each load–unload cycle transfers the loop's area to internal energy. A small loop wastes less and the tyre stays cooler.

questions.stem: Which treatment makes a copper wire harder to stretch permanently?

options.text: Heating it until its small grains grow into a few large ones
Hammering it cold, so that its dislocations multiply and tangle
Refining it to remove the few foreign atoms it contains
Stretching it a little within its elastic limit, then releasing it

questions.explanation: Tangled dislocations pin each other (work hardening). A larger stress is then needed for slip.
